title: Wheelbarrow
prompt: a miniature wheelbarrow carrying stones on a table with three buttons: “Load” adds stones to the tray; “Lift” raises the handles with the wheel as fulcrum; “Roll” carries the raised load forward; see-through reveals the wheel bearing and second-class lever geometry
blurb: A miniature teaching wheelbarrow shows how a load between wheel and handles reduces the effort needed to lift it.

identity.note: Levers / Second-class levers, page 20, and Wheelbarrow in Levers in action, page 22. Load lies between wheel fulcrum and handle effort.
identity.classificationNote: A named machine or diagram inside Levers is not a separate main chapter. The parking-meter heading is historical.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct load-carrying second-class application versus trolley. Nutcrackers and bottle-opener share the class but apply compression or cap removal.

prompt.note: Faithful. Load and Lift show force advantage. Roll is a secondary transport action. Show combined force at both handles, wheel support and actual load position. A bearing is a construction detail, not the reason handle effort is reduced.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

teachingAdaptation.initialState: Two 20 g stones in the tray and four on the table.

actions.Load: Transfers one visible stone over the lip into the lowered tray. Six-stone maximum.
actions.Lift: Raises or lowers both handles by rotating the frame 14 degrees about the wheel axle.
actions.Roll: Moves the lifted barrow 22 mm forward per press, at most twice on this finite table.

assumptions: Empty miniature barrow mass 160 g at model [66,40,32].
Handle force is the combined vertical quasi-static support force at both handles. Empty-frame moment is included.
The wheel supplies the remaining vertical support. Parked feet provide support, so the lifted force numbers are hidden when parked.
Stone transfer is a staged teaching action with no modeled human hand.
Arrows and dashed moment arms are drawn teaching overlays, excluded from anatomy.
Generic two-bearing hub with enlarged visible bearing details, not a reconstruction of the book illustration.

constructionSources.supports: Tray, tubular handles, grip sleeves, legs, cross brace, wheel, axle brackets, axle, bolts and washers.
Axle through hub, bearings at hub ends, brackets fixed to frame.
Representative deep-groove bearing inner and outer rings, ball and cage assembly.
